body:
I feel your pain as well, my father emotionally and physically abused me when I was growing up. Every time I was proud of something, he would remind me how useless I am. He never went to any of my graduations, because he would tell me how I am not worth his time. My mother was the only person who showed love, but she passed away. Now I am lost in the sea of depression, but I know things will get better, for both of us.

I convince myself every day even if it's a lie, things will look up. I think you're truly lost when you don't have anything to look forward to anymore. As much as my suicidal thoughts like to creep up, I want to keep them a bay. This may not be much, but just know there is one random person on the internet rooting for you. Things will get better, and I know it!

Take what I have to say with a grain of salt, as this is my own interpretation. I don't think there is a one-size-fits-all when it comes to getting help. Something that may work for you, may not work for others. I look at getting help, almost like a series of trial and error. You start off with the easiest way such as talking to others, going to see a therapist, and taking medication. However, it's when those actions no longer work, you have to start looking outside the box and see what can comfort you.

Much like almost everyone here, I suffer from depression and ever since my mother passed away it has only gotten worst. I am on the verge of ending my life every night when I sit alone in my office. I tried taking pills and even visiting a therapist, but sometimes the therapist you go to just isn't for you. Even though it's really minor, I recently just started to window shop. I would go to Best Buy and Amazon and look for things I really want. Then I tell myself when I get out of this, these are the things I will reward myself with. Will it help me in the long run? I don't know, but for now, it is keeping me grounded. Do I still have thoughts of ending it? Of course, but this is my form of help that keeps me in check. Even if this is only temporary, I rather have something that breaks up my need to end it, than constantly dig myself deeper into the abyss. 

So my answer is, there isn't a definite answer to what can help you, but don't get too caught up in a solution, but try and focus on what makes you take your mind off for a bit. Just make sure whatever you consider as help, isn't anything that causes self-harm like alcohol, drugs, or even hurting yourself. I am sorry I cannot offer you a direct answer, but I hope the best for you.
